title: PayrHealth notifies patients of breach of health data and Social Security numbers
date_note: The day the notice was reported to the California Attorney General (the register's Reported Date, 11/16/2026); the sample letter is also dated November 16, 2026. The letter says PayrHealth became aware of unauthorized activity on or around August 18, 2026.
geo_basis: mailing address given in the notice letter (2121 Lohmans Crossing Rd., Austin, TX 78734)
summary: PayrHealth, which provides healthcare revenue management services to medical providers, filed a breach notice with California's Attorney General. Its letter says it became aware of unauthorized activity in its systems on or around August 18, 2026, and that information was subject to unauthorized access for a limited period. Data may include names with addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, insurance and claims, and treatment or diagnosis information.
plain: A company that handles billing for medical providers says someone got into its systems in August 2026. Patients' Social Security numbers and medical details may have been exposed.
exec: Breach at a healthcare revenue management vendor exposed provider patients' health data and Social Security numbers.
action: PayrHealth's letter urges recipients to review account statements and explanation of benefits forms for suspicious activity and offers 12 months of credit monitoring through Cyberscout, with enrollment within 90 days.
impact: Number of people affected not stated in the notice or the register entry.

sources.name: California Attorney General: PayrHealth breach notification
PayrHealth sample notice letter (filed with the California AG)

report.publisher: PayrHealth (filed with the California Attorney General)
key_findings: On or around August 18, 2026, PayrHealth became aware of unauthorized activity within its computer systems.
Certain information within its systems was subject to unauthorized access for a limited period of time.
Data may include name with address, date of birth, Social Security number, member/patient identifier, insurance and claims information, and treatment or diagnosis information.
recommendations: Review account statements and explanation of benefits forms; enroll in the offered credit monitoring within 90 days.

evidence.quote: On or around August 18, 2026, we became aware of certain unauthorized activity within our computer systems.
Additionally, we are offering you complimentary credit monitoring and identity protection services for a period of 12 months.
In order for you to receive the monitoring services described above, you must enroll within 90 days from the date of this letter.

validation.note: Primary: PayrHealth's own notice letter, filed with and published by the California Attorney General (register entry sb24-633009, breach date 08/18/2026, reported 11/16/2026). No other publisher read.
